reproduction_target: Transcriptomic and DNA-methylation response of the grape phylloxera Daktulosphaira vitifoliae to experimental host transfer across nine grapevine genotypes. Computational target: RNA-seq QC (FastQC), trimming (BBTools bbduk), STAR alignment to the Rispe et al. 2020 D. vitifoliae reference and GeneCounts quantification, edgeR/limma-voom differential expression with the 'treat' 1.5-fold test, Fisher functional-group enrichment, DESeq2-vst + WGCNA signed co-expression network and module-eigengene/fitness regression, eggNOG-mapper KEGG assignment with clusterProfiler over-representation, ARGL protein BLASTp/Clustal Omega/WebLogo/iTOL sequence and phylogenetic analysis, and the WGBS arm: Trim Galore trimming, Bismark bisulfite mapping and deduplication, lambda-spike-in binomial methylated-CpG calling, bedtools feature annotation, prcomp PCA, methylKit differential methylation, and the transcriptional-plasticity vs methylation LOESS/Spearman/quartile-Wilcoxon analysis. Insect rearing, host-transfer infestation, gall/egg phenotyping, RNA and DNA extraction and Illumina NovaSeq library prep/sequencing are W (out of computational-reproduction scope).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML 'Materials and Methods' (sections s2a-s2j), retrieved by curl into /tmp/stage1_10.1101_2024.10.15.618594/paper.xml after WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403; title-phrase grep confirmed the correct paper. Code availability is a single sentence at the end of the DNA-methylation-analysis section: 'All scripts for data processing and bioinformatic analyses are available online at https://github.com/wcoll010/Grape-phylloxera-phenotypic-plasticity-during-host-transfer'. There is no separate Data availability or Code availability section; the two SRA statements are embedded in the RNA-sequencing and WGBS methods paragraphs. Repository landing page (unauthenticated GitHub API, stage-1 legal: file names only, no source read): root holds README.md plus one directory; that directory holds DV_fitness_analysis.R, RNAseq_preproccessing_alignment.txt, WGCNA_analysis_script.R, edgeR_DE_script_final.R, gene_set_enrichment.R and a 'BS-seq analysis' sub-directory with BSseq_preprocessing_alignment.txt, Fig5A_DNA_meth_per_sequence_context.txt, Fig5B_DNA_meth_per_genomic_feature.txt, Fig5C_FigS8_DV_CpG_methylation_PCA.txt, Fig5D_FigS9_DNA_meth_gene_expression_correlation.txt, methylKit_gene_differential_meth.txt. The README is two lines (repo name + paper title) with no install, dependency, run-order or figure-mapping text. No license, no release, no tag, no Zenodo/Software Heritage DOI (GitHub API /releases and /tags both return empty arrays; repo created 2025-09-18, last pushed 2025-11-19). The paper pins exact versions for many tools (FastQC 0.11.9, bbduk 38.95, STAR 2.7.10b, edgeR 4.0.16, DESeq2 1.42.1, pheatmap 1.0.12, ggplot2 3.5.0, clusterProfiler 4.10.1, Trim Galore 0.6.7, Bismark 0.24.1, bedtools 2.30.0, methylKit 1.28.0, R stats 4.3.1) but omits versions entirely for WGCNA and limma and gives only a bare major version for eggNOG-mapper ('v. 2') and iTOL ('v. 6'); web tools (NCBI BLASTp, Clustal Omega, WebLogo) carry no version at all. No lockfile, container, conda spec, renv.lock or sessionInfo is claimed anywhere in the paper or the repository landing page. 4 wet-lab steps counted in W and excluded from |S|. Stage-1 prose-only: no code was read line-by-line, no env_capture_class assigned.

steps.label: Wet-lab: establishment of a clonal D. vitifoliae line from a single female leaf gall on V. rupestris cv St. George (Davis CA, 2021) and maintenance on grafted/self-rooted V. vinifera cv Cabernet Sauvignon 33 in UC Riverside greenhouses (27 +/- 3 C), plus clonal propagation/potting of the nine grapevine host genotypes in UC Mix 3 at 24:27 C, 14 h photoperiod

Wet-lab: host-transfer infestation (G0 galled leaves placed on branch nodes, monitored every 12 h, removed after 2 days) and insect performance assay (4 mm hole-punch gall collection at 15/17/19/21/23 DPI, five largest galls per plant, eggs counted per gall under a dissecting microscope)

Wet-lab: RNA isolation from pools of 20 G1 adults per sample (RNeasy Mini Kit, Qiagen), QC by gel and spectrophotometry, NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA library prep, Illumina NovaSeq X sequencing at the UC Davis Genome Center (28.9 +/- 3.29 M paired-end reads per sample)

Wet-lab: CTAB DNA extraction (Mugford et al. 2020 method) from 200-250 pooled eggs or 15-20 adults per replicate, agarose/Qubit QC, 150 bp paired-end WGBS library prep and Illumina NovaSeq sequencing (UC Davis Genome Center for G1; Novogene for G0 eggs and adults; 47.2 +/- 1.20 M paired-end reads per sample), with lambda bacteriophage DNA spike-in

Insect fitness comparison across host grapevine genotypes: pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on eggs-per-gall counts, R v. 4.3.1 (repo script DV_fitness_analysis.R); the egg-count phenotype table itself is not deposited in any repository and is only implied to sit in the supplementary tables (supplements/618594_file02.xlsx)
Read and base quality statistics for raw and processed RNA-seq reads with FastQC v. 0.11.9 (https://github.com/s-andrews/FastQC), default settings
Quality trimming and filtering of raw RNA-seq reads with BBTools bbduk v. 38.95, default settings plus kmer length k=23 and hamming distance hist=1 (verbatim from Methods)

Alignment of trimmed RNA-seq reads to the D. vitifoliae reference genome (Rispe et al. 2020, cited by publication only) using STAR v. 2.7.10b with default settings plus --alignIntronMax 15000 and --outFilterIntronMotifs RemoveNoncanonical; only uniquely mapped reads retained
Gene count matrix generation with the STAR --quantMode GeneCounts option (STAR v. 2.7.10b), against the Rispe et al. 2020 annotation

Differential gene expression: edgeR v. 4.0.16 filterByExpr with default parameters, then limma voom + lmFit linear model fitting and the empirical-Bayes 'treat' test with a 1.5-fold-change filter and BH-adjusted p < 0.05 (limma itself is named without any version)
Construction of the host-responsive gene set: removal of genes differentially expressed between 'G1' Cab33 and 'G0' (same-host generational contrast) from all downstream host-responsive analyses

Gene functional-group enrichment by Fisher's exact test with the R stats package v. 4.3.1; significance at BH-adjusted p < 0.05 and odds ratio >= 2; functional groups defined from the published Rispe et al. 2020 genome annotation (repo script gene_set_enrichment.R)

Signed gene co-expression network with WGCNA (NO VERSION STATED) on genes with >= 0.5 CPM in at least four samples, counts normalised by DESeq2 vst v. 1.42.1, soft power beta = 16, hierarchical clustering on 1-TOM, module assignment via cutreeDynamic with minimum module size 20 and deepSplit 2 (repo script WGCNA_analysis_script.R)
Heat maps of module eigengenes and normalised expression (z-scores of vst-transformed counts) with pheatmap v. 1.0.12, rows clustered on Euclidean distance

Module-eigengene / fitness association: linear regression mean fitness = b0 + b1 x mean eigengene with the lm function of the R stats package v. 4.3.1, plotted with ggplot2 v. 3.5.0; depends on the same non-deposited egg-count fitness table as C1

KEGG term assignment to the predicted D. vitifoliae proteome with eggNOG-mapper 'v. 2' (major version only, no minor/build, no eggNOG database release, no --tax_scope or other options); 7,532 of 15,076 queried proteins annotated; no repository script covers this invocation

KEGG over-representation analysis with the 'enrich' function of the R package clusterProfiler v. 4.10.1 (hypergeometric test); significance at BH-adjusted p < 0.05 and gene count >= 4 (repo script gene_set_enrichment.R)

Identification of putative homologs of the D. vitifoliae ARabinoGalactan-Like (ARGL) proteins by BLASTp searches - no version, no database or database release, no e-value or other search parameters, no output table deposited, no script in the repository

Multiple sequence alignment of ARGL proteins and putative homologs with the Clustal Omega web application (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/jdispatcher/msa/clustalo) - hosted service, no version, no job identifier, no parameters, alignment file not deposited

Sequence logo visualisation of the alignment with the WebLogo web application (https://weblogo.threeplusone.com) - hosted service, no version, no parameters (units, composition adjustment, sequence range) stated

Phylogenetic tree construction from the Clustal Omega MSA output using the Interactive Tree of Life (iTOL) 'v. 6' web application (https://itol.embl.de) - major version only; no tree-inference method, substitution model, or support values stated, and no tree file deposited
Read and base quality statistics for raw and processed WGBS reads with FastQC version 0.11.9 (repo file BS-seq analysis/BSseq_preprocessing_alignment.txt)

WGBS read trimming with Trim Galore version 0.6.7, default parameters plus an 80 bp minimum read-length filter, followed by a second Trim Galore pass hard-clipping 25 bp from the 5' end and 20 bp from the 3' end of all reads to remove artifactual base composition

Bisulfite mapping of trimmed WGBS reads to the bisulfite-converted Rispe et al. 2020 reference genome with Bismark v. 0.24.1, followed by PCR-duplicate removal (59.4 +/- 0.71 % unique mapping; 17.7x +/- 5.59 genome coverage); alignment options beyond defaults are not stated

Extraction of genome-wide CpG, CHG and CHH methylation percentages per sample from the Bismark alignment reports and plotting with ggplot2 (Figure 5A; repo file Fig5A_DNA_meth_per_sequence_context.txt)

Calling of significantly methylated CpG sites by binomial test against the bisulfite non-conversion error rate (0.3% +/- 0, n=4, from spiked-in lambda bacteriophage DNA), filtered at BH-adjusted p < 0.001 (removes sites below ~10% methylation); R stats package v. 4.3.1

Annotation of CpG sites with gene information (gene ID, functional group) and genome features (UTRs, introns, exons, intergenic) using the 'intersect' command of bedtools v. 2.30.0 (Figure 5B; repo file Fig5B_DNA_meth_per_genomic_feature.txt)

Principal component analysis of global CpG methylation with prcomp (R stats package v. 4.3.1), restricted to CpG sites covered by >= 4 reads in all samples, methylated in at least one sample (binomial test, BH-adjusted p < 0.001) and with non-zero variance (Figure 5C / Figure S8)

Differential methylation testing across hosts with the R package methylKit v. 1.28.0 using logistic regression with an F-test, q-value cutoff 0.05 and a >= 10% methylation-difference cutoff (repo file methylKit_gene_differential_meth.txt)
Intersection of differentially methylated genes with host-responsive differentially expressed genes using the 'intersect' command of bedtools v. 2.30.0

Transcriptional plasticity vs DNA methylation: mean absolute log2 fold change over all host-by-host contrasts as the plasticity measure, per-gene methylation from the 'G0' adult samples, scatterplot with a fitted LOESS smoother (span and degree NOT stated) and a Spearman rank correlation test in the R stats package v. 4.3.1 (Figure 5D / Figure S9)
Binning of genes into quartiles by mean absolute log2 fold change followed by pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for differences in DNA methylation level between quartiles (R stats package v. 4.3.1)

headline.static_readiness: 0/28 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 22/28 computational steps. This paper is unusually well pinned for the corpus: 13 distinct tools carry exact prose version pins (FastQC 0.11.9, bbduk 38.95, STAR 2.7.10b, edgeR 4.0.16, DESeq2 1.42.1, pheatmap 1.0.12, ggplot2 3.5.0, clusterProfiler 4.10.1, Trim Galore 0.6.7, Bismark 0.24.1, bedtools 2.30.0, methylKit 1.28.0, R stats 4.3.1), parameters are stated at command-flag granularity for nearly every step, raw RNA-seq and WGBS reads are public at SRA BioProject PRJNA1211173 (52 runs, verified), and a public GitHub repository holds analysis scripts covering the fitness, RNA-seq preprocessing, edgeR DE, WGCNA, enrichment and all six BS-seq/figure steps. The 6 NI steps fall into two groups: (i) C9 WGCNA, whose package version is simply absent while every other package in the same script is pinned; (ii) the five sequence-analysis steps C12/C14-C17 (eggNOG-mapper 'v. 2', BLASTp, Clustal Omega, WebLogo, iTOL 'v. 6'), which are hosted or GUI tools run with major-version-only or no version, no parameters, no job identifiers, and no deposited intermediate alignment/tree files - none of them is covered by a repository script. Ceiling above RI is blocked for every step by the absence of any environment lock: no lockfile, no container, no conda spec, no renv.lock, no sessionInfo, and no release tag or archival DOI on the repository, so the exact pins cannot be resolved to a closed environment even under stage-2 execution.
headline.coverage: 28 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS 'Materials and Methods' (sections s2b-s2j). 4 wet-lab steps (clonal insect line establishment and grapevine propagation; host-transfer infestation and gall/egg performance assay; RNA extraction + NEBNext library prep + NovaSeq X sequencing; CTAB DNA extraction + WGBS library prep + NovaSeq sequencing) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 28/32 (88%) of enumerated steps.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment (all 28 computational steps); repository root README.md and the paper's single code-availability sentence
gaps.missing: Exact version pins exist for 13 tools but environment closure does not. The README is two lines long ('# Grape-phylloxera-phenotypic-plasticity-during-host-transfer' + the paper title) and names no dependency, no R version, no installation route. No renv.lock, environment.yml, conda-lock, requirements.txt, Dockerfile, image digest or sessionInfo() output is present in the repository listing or claimed in the paper. The R stats package is pinned at 4.3.1 but the Bioconductor release under which edgeR 4.0.16 / DESeq2 1.42.1 / clusterProfiler 4.10.1 / methylKit 1.28.0 were installed is not given, and no command-line tool is tied to a package manager or channel.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a resolved environment lock covering both stacks - a conda-lock/pixi.lock (or Dockerfile with an image digest) for FastQC/bbduk/STAR/Trim Galore/Bismark/bedtools/eggNOG-mapper, and an renv.lock plus sessionInfo() for the R/Bioconductor stack - commit it to the repository, and reference it from the code-availability sentence.

gaps.where: C9 (WGCNA), C6 (limma), C12 (eggNOG-mapper), C17 (iTOL), C14-C16 (BLASTp, Clustal Omega, WebLogo)
gaps.missing: WGCNA and limma are named with no version at all, even though every other package invoked in the same analyses is pinned. eggNOG-mapper is given as 'v. 2' and iTOL as 'v. 6' - bare major versions with no minor or build. BLASTp, Clustal Omega and WebLogo carry no version. WGCNA is the single reason step C9 (the co-expression network that anchors the paper's central 'thistle' module result) falls to NI rather than RI.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a versions table to Methods or Supplementary giving an exact version for WGCNA, limma, eggNOG-mapper (e.g. 2.1.12) with its eggNOG database release, iTOL, BLASTp (and the database release searched), and the Clustal Omega / WebLogo builds or job identifiers used.

gaps.where: Code repository state - github.com/wcoll010/Grape-phylloxera-phenotypic-plasticity-during-host-transfer (repo root; no immutable snapshot of the analysis-time code)
gaps.missing: The repository is public and live (HTTP 200) but has no release, no tag (GitHub API /releases and /tags both return empty arrays), no Zenodo or Software Heritage DOI, and no license file (license: null). The paper cites the bare repository URL, so the referenced code is whatever is on the floating 'main' branch; the repository was created 2025-09-18 and last pushed 2025-11-19, i.e. after the v1 preprint, and 19 commits have been made with no indication which commit produced the published figures.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release matching the submitted manuscript, archive it to Zenodo or Software Heritage to obtain a DOI, add a license, and cite the DOI (or at minimum the commit SHA) in the code-availability sentence instead of the bare repository URL.

gaps.where: Repository README.md and the overall run order across the 11 script/command files
gaps.missing: There is no run-order documentation and no mapping from scripts to results beyond the four 'Fig5*' filenames. The README contains no text past the title. The two preprocessing files (RNAseq_preproccessing_alignment.txt, BSseq_preprocessing_alignment.txt) are .txt command logs rather than executable scripts, so the boundary between them and the four .R scripts (DV_fitness_analysis.R, edgeR_DE_script_final.R, WGCNA_analysis_script.R, gene_set_enrichment.R) is undocumented, as is the handoff of intermediate files between them. Figures 1-4 and all supplementary figures other than S8/S9 have no named producing script.
gaps.how_to_close: Expand the README with an ordered run list, the expected input and output file for each script, and an explicit script-to-figure/table mapping; convert the .txt command logs into runnable shell scripts.

gaps.where: C4, C5, C8, C20, C23 (reference genome and annotation), C12/C13 (eggNOG and KEGG databases), C14 (BLASTp database)
gaps.missing: External reference resources are not pinned to immutable artifacts. The D. vitifoliae reference genome and its annotation - which also supply the 'functional groups' used in every enrichment test (C8) - are cited only as 'Rispe et al., 2020' with no accession, assembly version, GFF version or checksum. The eggNOG database release behind the 'precomputed orthology assignments' (C12) is not stated, nor is the KEGG release used by clusterProfiler (C13), nor the BLAST database and release searched for ARGL homologs (C14). All are moving targets that will not return the same 7,532/15,076 annotation counts on re-run.
gaps.how_to_close: Give the assembly accession and annotation file version (with checksums) for the Rispe et al. 2020 reference, state the eggNOG database release and the KEGG release/date, name the BLAST database and its release, and deposit the resulting annotation tables as supplementary files.

gaps.where: C14 (NCBI BLASTp web), C15 (Clustal Omega at ebi.ac.uk/jdispatcher/msa/clustalo), C16 (WebLogo at weblogo.threeplusone.com), C17 (iTOL at itol.embl.de)
gaps.missing: Four steps of the ARGL sequence-analysis arm depend entirely on hosted interactive web services whose state at run time is not recorded. No service version, no submission parameters, no job identifiers and no access dates are given, and none of the four steps is covered by a repository script. The 13-type dictionary has no hosted-service type; recorded as 11 (proprietary/uncontrolled dependency) with this qualification rather than silently dropped.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace or supplement the web-GUI runs with command-line equivalents (clustalo, blastp, weblogo, iqtree/raxml) whose versions and parameters can be pinned in a script, and deposit the resulting alignment, logo input matrix and tree files (Newick) as supplementary data.

gaps.where: C1 and C11 (insect fitness / eggs-per-gall phenotype data) and all intermediate matrices feeding C6-C13 and C22-C28
gaps.missing: Only raw sequencing reads are deposited. The eggs-per-gall fitness measurements that drive Figure 1, the C1 Wilcoxon tests and the C11 eigengene-fitness regressions are not deposited in any repository; the paper points to no accession for them and they are at best embedded in the supplementary workbook (supplements/618594_file02.xlsx). Likewise the STAR gene count matrix, the vst-transformed expression matrix, the module assignments, the per-CpG methylation calls and the methylKit result tables are not deposited, so any downstream step can only be started by re-running the full upstream pipeline from SRA.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the fitness phenotype table (per plant, per genotype, per DPI, per gall) and the key intermediates (gene count matrix, vst matrix, WGCNA module assignment table, filtered CpG methylation table) to Zenodo with checksums, and reference them from a proper Data availability section.

gaps.where: C12 (eggNOG-mapper), C14 (BLASTp), C15 (Clustal Omega), C16 (WebLogo), C17 (iTOL), and secondarily C20 (Bismark) and C27 (LOESS)
gaps.missing: Parameters are absent for the five sequence-analysis steps: no eggNOG-mapper options or taxonomic scope, no BLASTp e-value/database/query set, no Clustal Omega alignment options, no WebLogo settings, and - materially - no tree-inference method, substitution model or support statistic for the phylogeny, which the Methods attribute to iTOL even though iTOL is a visualisation tool and does not infer trees. Minor cases: Bismark is said to be run without stating any option beyond defaults, and the LOESS smoother in C27 has no span or degree.
gaps.how_to_close: State the full command line for each sequence-analysis step, name the actual tree-inference program and model used before iTOL visualisation, and record the LOESS span/degree and Bismark options.

gaps.missing: Insect rearing and grapevine propagation, host-transfer infestation and the gall/egg performance assay, and the two extraction + library prep + sequencing chains are physical steps and out of scope for computational reproduction (verdict X, excluded from |S| = 28). Recorded for completeness: the protocols are described at usable detail (genotypes, pot size, soil mix, temperature and photoperiod, DPI sampling schedule, kit names, read yields), and the sequencing outputs are deposited at PRJNA1211173. The one wet-lab-side item that does bear on the computational chain is the eggs-per-gall phenotype produced by W2, which is not deposited (see gap type 1).
gaps.how_to_close: n/a - OOS. Depositing the W2 phenotype table is what would connect this layer to the computational chain.
